title: Why Airbnb's CEO Measures Product Velocity, Not AI Tokens
content:
Airbnb's CEO says the company is shipping EIGHTY PERCENT MORE features. And he says measuring AI by tokens was NOT GOING TO WORK in the long run.
In an interview with Marina Mogilko, Brian Chesky said, quote, "I think the stat is that we're shipping 80% more features than a year ago. Most of it's because of AI."
That is Airbnb's own number, not an independent audit.
So how does a company know AI is working?
At the start of the year, he says, many CEOs told everyone to use AI, and measured it by how many tokens each person used.
There were even token leaderboards.
His verdict? For a couple of months, it may have been a good way to get people started.
But as a long-term strategy, he says it was clearly NOT GOING TO WORK.
Here is the line that matters.
Chesky said the customer DOES NOT CARE if you use AI to build your tools. They just want the product to be better and faster.
So Airbnb looks at PRODUCT VELOCITY instead. How fast are you shipping? How many features? Are they high quality, and are they successful?
He made one more point about competition.
In his words, the tools Airbnb has are the tools every company in the world has. We all have access to the exact same tools.
My read: the tools are not the edge. How you use them is.
So how do you apply this?
Step one. Stop reporting AI usage as a vanity number. Seats bought and prompts sent are inputs, not results.
Step two. Pick one outcome metric per team. For engineering, time from idea to release. For support, time to resolve a ticket.
Step three. Measure it before and after AI, for thirty days.
Imagine a support team that sends ten thousand prompts a month but resolves tickets no faster. That is cost, not progress.
Chesky put it this way. It is no longer, can you build it. It is, what do you build, and should you build it, and does it matter.
So pick outcomes worth measuring, and train your people to aim at them.
Here's my take.
If you cannot show what AI changed for your customer, you are not adopting AI. You are just PAYING FOR IT.
